name: Cyrene
overview: Cyrene was a significant city in Libya known for its Jewish community, which included a synagogue as mentioned in Acts 6:9. Scripture highlights individuals from Cyrene, such as Simon, who was compelled to bear Christ's cross (Mark 15:21), and Lucius, a teacher in the early church at Antioch (Acts 13:1). Believers from Cyrene were active in spreading the gospel, as seen when some traveled to Antioch to preach to the Grecians (Acts 11:20), demonstrating the city's role in the early Christian mission.
